taem (the 2006 guidance workbook's nominal Mach 2.5, 83,000 ft, 60 n mi; the text says 82,000 ft)
runway.widthM (the 1981 lakebed runway's width was not found) and runway.headingDeg (from the runway number)
touchdown.mainFt (wheels stopped 15,046 ft from the threshold after an 8,993 ft roll)
approach (the press kit's and the workbook's plan values: the 20 deg and 1.5 deg glideslopes, preflare at 2,000 ft, gear down at 250 ft; the flown values were not found)
entry.reversalsMach (Wikipedia, 'about'; no primary list of the Mach numbers was found, NASA says 'several roll reversals')
runway.lengthM (today's Rogers Dry Lake 05/23, 8.4 km; the 1981 length was not found)

provenance.l: NASA (2021): touchdown at MET 2 d 6 h 20 min 53 s; a 160 s deorbit burn on both OMS engines; entry interface 400,000 ft; about 16 min of blackout; 211 mph at touchdown; an 8,993 ft rollout

STS-1 Symposium (post-flight, NASA JSC): main gear about 3,100 ft long at 183 KEAS; nose gear 3,099 ft later at 5.6 ft/s sink; braking 5,952 ft after the mains; wheels stopped 15,046 ft from the threshold
STS-1 press kit (plan): deorbit ignition 53:28:00, entry interface 53:56:02, TAEM 54:21:30, landing 54:27:43; final approach on a 20 deg glide path, preflare at 2,000 ft, gear down at 250 ft
Entry, TAEM and Approach/Landing Guidance Workbook 21002 (2006): TAEM at about Mach 2.5, 60 n mi, 83 kft; 20 deg outer and 1.5 deg inner glideslopes, preflare about 2,000 ft
Wikipedia, STS-1: roll reversals at about Mach 18.5, 9.8, 4.8 and 2.8; landing on Runway 23 at Rogers Dry Lake
Wikipedia, Rogers Dry Lake: lakebed runway 05/23, 5.2 mi (8.4 km)
